sections.title: Reading Comprehension · Passage B
sections.intro: Read “Amazement Awaits” and answer questions 10–14. Vocabulary notes follow the poem.

passage.title: Amazement Awaits
passage.credit: —Maya Angelou · “Amazement Awaits,” from Maya Angelou: The Complete Poetry (2015), Random House

lines.text: *Written on the occasion of the 2008 Olympics at the request of the Olympic Committee*
Sheer amazement awaits
Amazement luxuriant in promise
Abundant in wonder
Our beautiful children arrive at this Universal stadium.
They have bathed in the waters of the world
And carry the soft silt of the Amazon, the Nile,
The Danube, the Rhine, the Yangtze and the Mississippi
In the palms of their right hands.
A wild tiger nestles in each armpit
And a meadowlark perches on each shoulder.
We, the world audience, stand, arms akimbo,¹
Longing for the passion of the animal:
The melody of the lark
And the tigers’ passion
Attend the opening bells,
The birds sing of the amazement which awaits.
The miracle of joy that comes out of the gathering of our best,
bringing their best,
Displaying the splendor of their bodies and the radiance of their
agile minds to the cosmos.
Encouragement to those other youth caught in the maws² of poverty,
Crippled by the terror of ignorance.
They say,
Brothers and Sisters,
Yes, try.
Then try harder.
Lunge forward, press eagerly for release.
The amazement which awaits is for you.
We are here at the portal of the world we had wished for
At the lintel³ of the world we most need.
We are here roaring and singing.
We prove that we can not only make peace, we can bring it with us.
With respect for the world and its people,
We can compete passionately without hatred.
With respect for the world and its people,
We can take pride in the achievement of strangers.
With respect for the world and its people,
We can share openly in the success of friends.
Here then is the Amazement:
Against the odds of impending war,
In the mouth of bloody greed,
Human grace and human spirit can still conquer.
Ah…
We discover, we ourselves
Are the Amazement which awaits
We are ourselves Amazement.
¹ akimbo — with hands on hips and elbows turned outward
² maws — jaws
³ lintel — a horizontal support above a door or window

questions.prompt: The first stanza sets a tone of
questions.explanation: The stanza declares that “amazement awaits” as athletes arrive at the stadium. Its focus on wonders still to come creates anticipation.

questions.prompt: The figurative language in lines 5 through 8 emphasizes the
questions.explanation: The competitors symbolically carry silt from rivers across several continents. The global river imagery emphasizes how diverse the Olympic participants are.

questions.prompt: Lines 21 through 28 suggest that one impact the Olympics may have is to

choices.text: provide an inspiration to all people
emphasize the courage of all people

questions.explanation: The athletes’ example encourages other young people, including those facing poverty, to try and keep trying. Their achievements can inspire people beyond the stadium.

questions.prompt: The poet uses repetition in lines 33 through 38 in order to
questions.explanation: Repeating “With respect for the world and its people” before examples of fair competition and shared success reinforces the poem’s theme of unity through respect.

questions.prompt: Which line in the poem best illustrates the symbolism of “Amazement” in the last stanza?

choices.text: “Our beautiful children arrive at this Universal stadium” (line 4)
“Longing for the passion of the animal” (line 12)
“Human grace and human spirit can still conquer” (line 42)

questions.explanation: The last stanza reveals that people themselves are the “Amazement.” The earlier line about human grace and spirit overcoming war and greed best explains that symbol of human possibility.
